reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that Al and Ti additions to a Ni-Co-Fe-Cr HEA create a γ+γ’ structure that improves thermal stability and strength, but this is in a Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti system, not a Ti-Ni primary HEA. The key premise that a γ’ phase can form in a Ti-Ni primary matrix and that 3–5 at% Al alone will induce it is unsupported by the cited passages, which describe a different base alloy and include Ti as a co-addition.
premises: Al addition to Ni-based superalloys promotes γ’ precipitate formation
γ’ precipitates are coherent and ordered FCC structures
γ’ precipitates enhance high-temperature strength and creep resistance
The proposed Ti-Ni primary HEA can form a γ’ phase analogous to Ni-based superalloys
